analysis.title: Inflation prints cement December hike (Across the Americas)
key_insights: October headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and core CPI 0.3% m/m, both slightly above expectations. It was the third straight month of higher inflation readings, and core rounding to 0.3% is called unacceptably high for the Fed.
Core goods, housing and core services ex-housing were all lower than in September, and the 6m annualized core rate improved to 2.7% from 2.9%.

October headline PPI was slightly cooler than consensus and well below September. Core PPI was in line and lower than the prior month. Combined with CPI, the PCE deflator is unlikely to make meaningful progress toward target, which Natixis says cements a December hike.

Natixis leans toward a 25bp hike in December and perhaps another in March. It argues the Fed risks falling behind the curve by not acting decisively, though this FOMC has signaled a gradual, cautious path.

Governor Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered if October core CPI came in around 0.3% or higher. Core rounded to 0.3%, which brings a larger December hike into play, though Natixis expects the rest of the FOMC not to share his view.
Dallas Fed President Logan said inflation is trending meaningfully above target and called for at least two more 25bp hikes. She said it may be possible to move more rapidly this winter.
The Fed published a revised 2027 FOMC schedule. There are still eight meetings, but the October 2027 meeting will be devoted solely to monetary policy discussions with no decision.

NFIB small business optimism slipped to 97.8 from 97.9, below the 98.2 expected. The net share planning further price increases over the next three months rose 6 points to 37%, the highest since July 2022.

Rates strategy: Waller's 50bp comment plus the 0.3% core print produced a significant bear flattening this week, without relief from tech weakness. Pricing now peaks at an additional 89bps of hikes through September 2027.
Natixis is cautious about buying this dip. It sees no clear catalyst to reduce Fed pricing before December, and a soft PCE would be little reason to take out hikes after a third poor CPI report.

The desk still prefers owning the long end for 2027 and sees about 5.25% on 10s as a solid medium-term level. It would look to buy 10s at 5.00% or above, ideally against 5.20%, but wants to see why yields are there rather than leave a resting order.

Risk: if data stay strong and the Fed hikes only 25bp with 50bp under discussion, the bear flattening could become a bear steepening, as in July 2026 after Warsh's presser. This would likely need another strong payroll report.

AI buildout note: issuance plus hedging may have added about $530mm dv01 of pressure on US rates in 2026, rising to about $750mm dv01 in 2027, versus about $950mm dv01 of 10yr+ Treasury issuance a year.
Using Fed QE studies, Natixis estimates the $530mm dv01 could have pushed 10yr yields up about 45bps in 2026, ceteris paribus.

Hyperscaler off-balance-sheet lease funding is hedged with pay-fixed swaps. This reversed the historical link between IG issuance and swap spreads, leaving 10y swap spreads about 12bp higher than historical issuance would imply.
Natixis expects 2027 AI activity to disappoint relative to market expectations (in some cases about +40%) because it only needs to not accelerate as much, not slow, to give rates relief.

Brazil: the government's PLP 299/2026 fiscal framework proposal caps real spending growth at 2% (from 2.5%) and targets the midpoint of the primary balance range, implying 0.5% of GDP in 2027. Savings are estimated at R$50-60bn (about 0.40% of GDP), and the government says it may aim for R$80bn. Natixis says the exceptions make the framework complicated and unconvincing to the market.

Peru: the BCRP raised its policy rate 25bp to 4.50%, in line with consensus. October inflation was 5.25% vs 4.55% in September, and 12-month expectations are 3.1%. Natixis expects a pause in December, the next hike in January or February, and a peak in the 4.75-5.00% range.

tension_points.bull_case: Natixis favors the long end for 2027, sees 5.20% as good value and about 5.25% as solid medium-term, and expects 2027 AI activity to disappoint.
tension_points.bear_case: No near-term catalyst to reduce Fed pricing, a third poor CPI in a row, and Waller's 50bp talk leaves hike risk priced in, so yields could rise further.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another strong payroll report with a 25bp-only Fed hike while 50bp is discussed could turn the bear flattening into a bear steepening, as in July 2026.
